2611.20940.title: Gravitational Potential of CALIFA Galaxies from the Blue Cloud to the Red Sequence
2611.20940.text: We explore the gravitational potential of 238 (E1$-$Sdm) CALIFA galaxies from the Blue cloud to the Red Sequence using the star formation rate$-$stellar mass diagram ($\mathrm{SFR}-M_\star$) diagnosis. On average, galaxies in the Blue cloud possess slow-rising circular velocity curves (CVCs), those in the Green valley have flat CVCs, while galaxies in the Red sequence are characterised with peaked CVCs. Both the maximum circular velocity ($V_{c,\mathrm{max}}$) and asymptotic circular velocity ($V_{c,\mathrm{flat}}$) of the galaxies increase from the Blue cloud to the Red sequence, and show approximately linear relations with the logarithmic offsets from the star-forming main sequence ($Δ\mathrm{SFR}$s). The $Δ\mathrm{SFR}-\log_{10}(V_{c,\mathrm{max}})$ relation has a steeper slope ($-0.154 \pm 0.012$) than the $Δ\mathrm{SFR}-\log_{10}(V_{c,\mathrm{flat}})$ relation ($-0.124 \pm 0.011$).

2611.20919.title: Cosmological Collider Signals from Fermion Bubble Loops with a Chemical Potential
2611.20919.text: We present the first systematic analytical calculation of the local and nonlocal cosmological collider (CC) signals generated by massive fermion bubble loops in the presence of an effective chemical potential during inflation. Working in the de Sitter approximation, we investigate the four-point correlator of inflaton perturbations in the single-squeezed limit. By combining CC cutting rules, late-time expansions, and partial Mellin-Barnes (MB) techniques, we derive analytical expressions for both local and nonlocal signals. In particular, we identify two distinct contributions to the local signal, arising from spectrum and integer poles and from ultraviolet poles of the loop-momentum integral. We further investigate the three-point limit, where the separately extracted local and nonlocal contributions develop apparent folded singularities. By reorganizing the MB representation, we demons

2611.20917.title: The LAMOST Galaxy Parameter Catalog (LAGC): Stellar Populations, Kinematics, and Emission Lines of Galaxies in the LAMOST Spectroscopic Survey
2611.20917.text: The LAMOST Galaxy Parameter Catalog (LAGC) is a value-added data product of the LAMOST spectroscopic survey, generated by an automated spectral-fitting pipeline and released as a continuously updated catalogue series. Despite the vast data volume of the LAMOST spectroscopic survey, no dedicated, homogeneous pipeline had previously been able to extract stellar population, kinematic, and emission-line information simultaneously from its galaxy spectra, primarily because of the poorly controlled absolute flux calibration and a line spread function (LSF) that varies with wavelength, fibre, and time. The pipeline addresses both challenges through the SEW full-spectrum fitting method, which operates in equivalent-width space and is therefore immune to multiplicative flux-calibration errors, together with an accurate, wavelength-dependent model of the LAMOST LSF that enables unbiased kinematic

2611.20910.title: Galaxy number counts in area distance space
2611.20910.text: We investigate how galaxy clustering changes when area distance is used as the radial coordinate. We derive the linear relativistic number counts for a flux-selected population and compare them with redshift and luminosity distance space. Source motion does not change the beam area at a fixed emission event, so area-distance clustering has no Kaiser distortion. Lensing changes both the angular and radial positions of sources, and can enhance area-distance clustering while weakening its correlation with redshift-space clustering. Observer motion shifts area-distance shells in the opposite direction to redshift and luminosity-distance shells, allowing their kinematic dipoles to point in opposite directions. A combination of the three count fields cancels their common intrinsic density and explicit evolution and magnification biases, leaving a signal dominated by velocities nearby and optic

2611.20884.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
2611.20884.text: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\si

2611.20828.title: LAMOST III Low-resolution Spectroscopic Survey: Overview and Target Selection
2611.20828.text: We present an overview of the LAMOST III Low-resolution Spectroscopic Survey (LRS), including its scientific goals, target selection strategy, and current observing status. Targets in the main survey are selected via weighted random sampling, using the inverse local density in the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram and in the G-magnitude distribution, with additional enhancement in selected regions of the HR diagram. The main survey is complemented by 35 dedicated add-on catalogs (including very metal-poor star candidates, halo stars, hot/young stars, wide binaries, extragalactic sources and so on) and a time-domain program providing multi-epoch spectroscopy of binaries and other peculiar systems. LAMOST III LRS is designed to map the structure and evolution of the Galactic disk, reconstruct the assembly and early chemical-enrichment history of the Galactic halo, improve stellar-parameter

2611.20672.title: The Effect of Asphericity to the Inference of Supernova Circumstellar Environment from Radio Observations
2611.20672.text: Radio observations of supernovae (SNe) enable us to constrain the circumstellar environment of their progenitor stars, and hence the mass-loss history immediately prior to the explosion. However, despite lines of evidence pointing to the aspherical configurations of circumstellar matter (CSM) around many SNe, the derivation of CSM parameters is often done under the assumption of spherically symmetric CSM. In this work, based on a recent model of radio emission from SNe interacting with aspherical CSM, we investigate how lifting the assumption of spherical symmetry affects the CSM parameter inference. First, we apply the model to mock data simulating typical observations of Type Ia-CSM, Ibc and II SNe and find that the total CSM mass required for to reproduce radio observation depends weakly on the CSM covering fraction $f_Ω$, with ${f_Ω}^{0.15-0.38}$. We then apply the model and fit the

2611.20669.title: Long-Term Radio Evolution of the Type Ia Supernova SN 2020eyj: Evidence for a Dense Helium-rich Circumstellar Shell
2611.20669.text: The nature of progenitor systems of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) and their explosion mechanism remain controversial. Radio observations provide a powerful probe of the interaction between SN ejecta and circumstellar material (CSM), offering important constraints on the mass-loss histories of their progenitor systems. We present extensive Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) observations of SN 2020eyj at 1.5-10 GHz, tracing its radio emission to approximately 1300 days after discovery and revealing, for the first time, the long-term radio evolution of an SN Ia. The radio light curves of SN 2020eyj exhibit a relatively flat evolution at early epochs, followed by a gradual long-term decline, while its radio spectra show a power-law behavior with a low-frequency turnover. These characteristics appear to be consistent with synchrotron emission associated with shock interaction. Modeling the radio li

2611.20636.title: Ca II IRT activity indices from $Gaia$ spectroscopy: a baseline method for photospheric contribution estimates
2611.20636.text: The $Gaia$ high-resolution spectroscopic observations using Radial Velocity Spectrometer offers a unique opportunity to study stellar Ca II infrared triplet (IRT) activity. A key step in estimating activity indices is subtracting the photospheric contribution. The canonical template-based method often fails because, for many stars, the observed line cores are deeper than the model predictions, which prevents valid activity measurements. In this work, we explore an alternative approach that constructs a baseline from less active stars as a function of effective temperature (and metallicity) to represent the photospheric contribution. Our results show that, for dwarf stars, compared with the canonical method, the baseline method not only yields far more objects with valid activity measurements, but also avoids many extremely low and unreliable values (e.g., log$R'_{\rm IRT} \lesssim -6$).

2611.20633.title: Model-Driven Stellar Spectroscopy with the Total Differential Spectral Model (TDSM): Framework and Its Application to 11 Million LAMOST Low-Resolution Spectra
2611.20633.text: Deriving stellar astrophysical parameters from large-scale spectroscopic surveys requires accurate modeling of spectra across a wide wavelength coverage and a broad range of stellar parameter space, which remains a great challenge. In this work, we present \texttt{TDSM}, a physically motivated neural network architecture that self-consistently emulates both the flux and its first-order derivative of the ab initio stellar spectra. The method enables accurate and precise emulation of Kurucz synthetic spectra with severely blended features at $R \simeq 2000$ in a high-dimensional parameter space, achieving a typical pixel-wise flux precision of 0.05\% in the wavelength range $3700<λ<9000$Å over the parameter range of $3000 < T_{\rm eff} < 45,000$~K, $-1 < \log g < 5$, and $-4.0 < \mathrm{[Fe/H]} < 0.5$. The model is applied to LAMOST DR10 to derive stellar parameters for 11 million spectra

2611.20418.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
2611.20418.text: A new epoch for direct visualisation of accretion dynamics near a black hole's event horizon began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (EHTC) synthesised an Earth-sized aperture with millimeter radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features, with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source. Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very-long baseline interferometry (VLBI) measurements, renderin

2611.20416.title: Repeated Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Binary Black Holes on Eccentric and Precessing Orbits around Spinning Supermassive Black Holes
2611.20416.text: Gravitational waves (GWs) from a stellar-mass binary black hole (BBH) orbiting a supermassive black hole (SMBH) can experience repeated gravitational lensing as the BBH passes behind the SMBH. Our previous studies of orbit-induced GW modulation motivate this investigation of repeated lensing in evolving hierarchical triple systems. We investigate how eccentricity, inclination, and relativistic precession of the outer orbit affect successive lensing events and parameter inference. The outer orbit follows post-Newtonian dynamics, and the inspiral waveform includes moving-source effects and de Sitter precession. An event-local point-mass lensing model tracks the changing source--lens alignment and GW frequency. For a one-year LISA observation, we examine lensing-event identification, Fisher-matrix estimates of parameter uncertainties, and waveform residuals when lensing is omitted. Our resu

2611.20358.title: Tracing the Luminosity Evolution of Globular Cluster Systems with JWST: MACS J1149.5+2223 at z=0.544
2611.20358.text: We present a study of the compact-source population associated with the massive galaxy cluster MACS J1149.5+2223 at z=0.544 using deep JWST/NIRCam imaging in F115W, F150W, and F200W. After photometric and morphological selection, we identify 1,202 unresolved compact-source candidates. The observed luminosity distribution samples only the bright side of the expected globular-cluster luminosity function (GCLF), remaining several magnitudes above the turnover. Based on published GCLF turnovers for Abell 2744 and MACS 0417, we adopt an expected turnover magnitude of m_0=33.66 mag for MACS 1149. A forward-modeled fit then yields sigma=1.71 mag, which characterizes the observed bright-side slope under the adopted turnover rather than the intrinsic width of the full GCLF. Comparison with PARSEC simple stellar population models shows that the elevated luminosities of the compact sources are cons

2611.20356.title: Triple Exchange at the Cosmological Collider in Closed Form
2611.20356.text: Particles with masses near the Hubble scale leave a characteristic pattern in the primordial bispectrum, turning inflation into a cosmological collider. For light fields, where this signal is largest, no closed form is known for the full shape of the quasi-single-field triple exchange. Using Feynman-integral methods, we obtain the first closed-form results, exact in the momenta, as expansions in terms of multiple polylogarithms around the massless and conformally coupled limits. We show that the template used in Planck analyses overestimates the amplitude by up to a factor of 1.8 and underestimates the mass, whereas our new template recovers both, as needed for current and upcoming CMB and galaxy surveys. We also compute the collapsed trispectrum and, combining it with the bispectrum, find that at weak mixing it bounds the self-coupling more tightly.

2611.20302.title: Population structure of the velocity distribution in normal shock waves: Gaussian representations, Mach-number similarity, and prediction
2611.20302.text: Normal shock waves are commonly described as mixtures of upstream and downstream Maxwellians. Discrete-velocity solutions of three relaxation models up to Mach 12 and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) of hard-sphere and variable-hard-sphere gases up to Mach 25 are used to examine the population structure, Mach-number similarity and upstream precursor of their velocity distributions. Three anisotropic Gaussian populations reproduce the streamwise reduced distributions of the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model and of DSMC to within 4\% up to Mach 12, and of DSMC to within 6\% at Mach 25, whereas two Maxwellians incur errors up to 50\% (BGK) and 37\% (DSMC). Collision histories identify the hard-sphere beam with unscattered stream molecules, which carry half of the peak viscous stress; the other populations are effective descriptions, not collision classes. Above Mach 5, Rankine--Hugoni

2611.20236.title: Unveiling the Multi-Phase Outflow in NGC 4151 with JWST Observations - I. Integrated Properties of the Outflow
2611.20236.text: The biconical outflow of the nearby Seyfert 1.5 AGN NGC 4151 has been studied across the electromagnetic spectrum, yet mapping its multiphase structure with a single facility has remained challenging. Leveraging the broad wavelength coverage of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), we present new near- and mid-infrared observations tracing the ionization stratification of these outflows with a unified dataset. We analyze emission lines originating from molecular gas to highly ionized plasma and analyze the ionized gas using a 5-component Cloudy photoionization model covering three primary phases. Applying the footprint line method to characterize the X-ray emitting gas, we find that it holds the largest share of the total mass, suggesting that it is a primary candidate for driving AGN feedback in this system.

2611.20166.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Double-source-plane lens candidates
2611.20166.text: Strong gravitational-lensing systems with multiple source planes are powerful tools for probing the stellar and dark matter content of galaxies. Lens modelling can measure the relative Einstein radii of the two source planes, which encode a ratio of angular-diameter distances determined by the lens and source redshifts and the dark energy equation of state, independently of the Hubble constant. Galaxy-scale double-source-plane lenses (DSPLs) are extremely rare. We present a sample of 84 galaxy-scale DSPL candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), of which 80 are newly identified. These systems were selected using machine-learning lens-finding models followed by visual inspection by citizen scientists and experts. We then used lens modelling to test the DSPL interpretation. Among our lens candidates, 11 form the 'Gold' sample: each shows two sets of multiple images at different radii, and

2611.20141.title: The mass density slope of early-type galaxies: newest results from the redshift distribution of strong gravitational lenses
2611.20141.text: The mass distribution of early-type galaxies (ETGs) encodes key information about baryonic processes and dark-matter assembly. In this paper, we propose a new framework to investigate the mass-density profiles of ETGs and their evolution with redshift, based on the redshift distribution of strong gravitational lenses. We compile 200 galaxy-scale strong lensing systems with complete information, including lens and source redshifts, Einstein radii, and spectroscopic velocity dispersions. To account for the heterogeneous construction of the compiled sample, we model a lens-redshift-dependent selection function for each survey category. By combining the lens-redshift distribution with velocity dispersion function (VDF) and spherical Jeans-based mapping, we obtain population-level constraints on the total mass-density slope gamma in three lens-redshift intervals, marginalizing over the lumino

2611.19906.title: Magnetic fields in blazar jets derived from synchrotron self-absorption
2611.19906.text: Context. Magnetic fields are believed to play a crucial role in the launching, acceleration, and evolution of blazar jets. However, direct measurements of the magnetic field strength in the radio-emitting regions of blazar jets remain limited. Aims. We aim to estimate the magnetic field strengths in the synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) regions of blazar jets and investigate their connections with the properties of the jet and central engine. Methods. We compiled multifrequency radio data for 143 blazars and fitted their radio spectra with a combined power-law and SSA model to derive the turnover frequency and turnover flux density. The magnetic field strengths were then calculated by combining the SSA parameters with the very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) measured angular sizes and Doppler factors compiled from the literature. Results. The SSA-derived magnetic fields are systemati

2611.19899.title: Towards the LSST DESC pipeline for cosmology with galaxy clusters -- design and validation on simulations
2611.19899.text: We present the current implementation of an automated framework developed within the Legacy Survey of Space and Time Dark Energy Science Collaboration (LSST DESC) for galaxy cluster cosmology, in preparation for the first LSST data releases of the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The cluster cosmology pipeline integrates DESC-developed tools dedicated to galaxy/cluster catalog ingestion, cluster number count and weak lensing measurements, modeling, and parameter inference through posterior sampling, enabling reproducible end-to-end cluster cosmology analyses. We test and validate the pipeline using synthetic mock datasets and the LSST DESC cosmoDC2 simulation, performing a joint analysis of redMaPPer cluster abundance and stacked weak lensing profiles measured in bins of redshift and richness. We constrain two cosmological parameters, $Ω_c$ and $σ_8$, along with six cluster mass-observ

2611.19884.title: Mock Observations: Morphological Analysis of Galactic Bars in IllustrisTNG Simulations
2611.19884.text: Galactic bars are important tracers of disk-galaxy evolution, yet reported bar fractions vary among observational studies and between observations and cosmological simulations. We compare bar statistics and properties in the IllustrisTNG simulations(TNG100 and TNG50 at z~0.1) with Sloan Digital Sky Survey(SDSS) galaxies at0.1<=z<=0.1264. We generate synthetic r-band TNG images,match SDSS observational conditions,and analyze mock TNG and real SDSS images using a common image-based framework of source segmentation,morphological classification, and isophotal ellipse fitting. For face-on late-type galaxies with log(M*/Msun)>10,the global bar fractions are 26.68+/-0.23%,24.96(-.76/+.78)%, and 13.42(-1.07/+1.15)% for SDSS,TNG100,and TNG50,respectively. 2611.19867.title: Stripped White Dwarfs as Spectroscopic Clocks: Abundance Transitions in Partial Tidal Disruptions
2611.19867.text: We investigate partial tidal disruptions of He and CO white dwarfs (WDs) by a $10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We construct realistic WD structures and abundance profiles with MESA and map them into FLASH to follow the remnant response and the time-dependent composition of the fallback debris in single pericentre passages on tightly bound orbits ($e=0.9$). The element-specific fallback rates exhibit pre-peak compositional transitions that trace the WD's stratified layers. In the grazing encounter ($β=0.55$), hydrogen dominates the earliest returning debris, followed by helium, showing a H$\rightarrow$He transition. Deeper encounters ($β=0.7$ and $0.8$) penetrate the CO core and produce a He$\rightarrow$C transition, that occurs earlier relative to peak fallback and is stronger in the deeper encounter. These signatur

2611.19721.title: Magnetogenesis in Low-Scale Inflation: Viability for Astrophysical Magnetic Fields
2611.19721.text: The indirect evidence for magnetic fields in the intergalactic medium motivates the study of their possible primordial origin, including generation during inflation. One mechanism for inflationary magnetogenesis involves a pseudoscalar inflaton coupled to a gauge field through the interaction $g_{φγ}φF_{μν}\tilde{F}^{μν}$. In this work, we study the viability of this mechanism in the context of low scale inflation, particularly on inflationary energy scales near the electroweak (EW) scale. We find that the post inflationary amplification of the gauge fields can produce astrophysically relevant magnetic fields for $g_{φγ}\ge 360~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$ in the absence of Schwinger backreaction for an inflationary scale around the EW scale. We then include the backreaction of the charged current generated through the Schwinger mechanism. We find that the induced current suppresses the gauge field

2611.19631.title: Orion I: Discovery of an Isolated dE,N Galaxy at 60 Mph
2611.19631.text: Inspection of deep JWST images centered on the lensing cluster of galaxies MACS J0454.1-0300 reveals a small, well resolved stellar system that is clearly in the foreground. Photometric measurements including a color-magnitude diagram and radial profile show that it is a nucleated dwarf early-type galaxy (dE,N) at a distance of ~60 Mpc and with structurally normal properties. This object (J04:54:07.39-02:59:22.5, referred to as Orion I for shorthand) may be an outlying member of a previously known small galaxy group, or may be simply an isolated field galaxy depending on the accuracy of its distance estimate. The discovery of Orion I suggests that other small stellar systems in the nearby universe might be found through a search of the many deep \jwst imaging fields that are now being accumulated.

2611.19491.title: Unbound matter in the circum-halo medium: a common mediator of halo secondary bias
2611.19491.text: Halo secondary bias describes the dependence of halo clustering on properties beyond mass. Here we report that a new environmental metric, the unbound matter fraction ($f_{\rm un}$) in the $2$--$3\,R_{\rm vir}$ shell around a halo, can largely account for secondary bias. Using haloes with $M_{\rm vir}=10^{10.5}$--$10^{14.5}h^{-1}{\rm M_\odot}$ at $z=0$ obtained from TNG300-1-Dark, we find that controlling for $f_{\rm un}$ reduces the secondary bias of formation time, concentration, spin, shape and velocity anisotropy to a residual correlation of $\lesssim 4\%$, outperforming other environmental metrics such as the tidal anisotropy for spin and velocity anisotropy. Applying a stacking method to the circum-halo medium (CHM), we identify two distinct flow patterns: low-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes co-move with coherent flows, with the CHM converging onto the haloes; in contrast, high-$f_{\rm un}$ ha

2611.19416.title: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
2611.19416.text: The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. In the $Λ$CDM+$\sum m_ν$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_ν<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino

2611.19391.title: Lindblad and Corotation Resonances as the Common Origin of Moving Groups, Diagonal Ridges, and Velocity Waves in the Milky Way Disc
2611.19391.text: The Galactic disc is a complex dynamical system showing various kinematic structures, including moving groups (MGs), diagonal ridges (DRs), and velocity waves. To investigate their possible dynamical connection, we analyzed the phase-space distribution of stars from the extit{Gaia} DR3 catalog. We used angular momentum $L_z$ as a key dynamical tracer and examined stellar densities and velocities as functions of $L_z$. We identified stellar groups at specific $L_z$-values and associated them with extrema in the median radial velocity $\left<V_R ight>$, known as a velocity wave. By cross-matching the extrema of the $\left<V_R ight>$-wave with structures in the $V_R$--$L_z$ and $R$--$L_z$ planes, we established a clear connection between the velocity wave, the main MGs, and the DRs. A similar connection was partially identified for corrugations in the median vertical velocity $\left<V_z igh

2611.19327.title: Unveiling Hidden X-ray Broad Line Region in Centaurus A: Broadband Analysis with XRISM and NuSTAR
2611.19327.text: We present a broadband X-ray spectral analysis of the radio galaxy Centaurus~A, utilizing simultaneous \textit{XRISM} (Resolve and Xtend) and \textit{NuSTAR} observations. Unlike the previous phenomenological analysis of the Fe K$α$ line (Bogensberger et al. 2025), we employ physical reflection models developed with the radiative transfer code SKIRT. They self-consistently predict the continuum and fluorescent lines from a clumpy torus and an X-ray broad line region (xBLR). The Fe K$α$ complex is well reproduced with a three velocity component model. We interpret this as two narrow torus components (FWHM $= 310\pm50$ and $1900\pm400$~km~s$^{-1}$) and an xBLR component (FWHM $= 6000_{-800}^{+1100}$~km~s$^{-1}$). The inner torus radius of 0.13~pc is 10 times the dust sublimation radius (0.013~pc), implying that the torus in a low-luminosity AGN is not determined by dust-related physics. Th

2611.19308.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
2611.19308.text: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<z<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpostσ$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipostσ$ and lies $\vnsplan

2611.19294.title: Initial Conditions Dictate Gas-Stellar Counter-Rotation in Galaxies
2611.19294.text: We present a physical origin of gas-stellar counter-rotation in galaxies. Scale-dependent partitions of tidal torques from cosmic primordial perturbations source angular momentum for distinct baryonic components. This scale dependence maps to radial hierarchy in Lagrangian space clustering: stellar components, assembled at earlier times from the inner protohalo, retain persistent memory of small-scale tidal torques, whereas gas, accreted later from outer Lagrangian regions, is governed by large-scale perturbations and can develop counter-rotation. This mechanism is observationally testable and offers a direct probe of the hierarchical cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm. Unlike conventional late-time scenarios that only explain the existence of counter-rotation, our framework further predicts its component-resolved direction, enabling component-resolved angular momentum to serve as a new pro

2611.19211.title: From Non-parametric Statistics to Images: Generating Galaxy Morphologies
2611.19211.text: Non-parametric statistics characterize complex galaxy morphologies but do not specify how to construct images that reproduce those statistics. We present Flow-VAE, which combines a variational autoencoder with a conditional normalizing flow to generate images conditioned on concentration, asymmetry, smoothness (CAS), Gini coefficient (G), and M20. A Gaussian mixture model completes unspecified descriptors and measures the training-distribution support of requested combinations. Using a dataset of 240,000 DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys r-band images, we evaluate fidelity by remeasuring morphological statistics from model outputs and comparing them with the inputs. With a tolerance of +/-10% of each descriptor's adopted range, descriptor-specific recovery rates are 96.62-99.97% for reconstruction and 87.81-99.83% for single-parameter generation among valid measurements. Generated descriptors

2611.19134.title: OGLE-2018-BLG-0829L: A Microlensing System with a Planet Orbiting a Star Possessing a Brown-Dwarf Companion
2611.19134.text: We analyze the microlensing event OGLE-2018-BLG-0829, whose light curve exhibits a weak short-term anomaly in addition to the prominent caustic-crossing features of a binary lens. The anomaly cannot be explained by a binary-lens single-source (2L1S) model. We therefore investigate both binary-lens binary-source (2L2S) and triple-lens single-source (3L1S) interpretations and find that both models reproduce the additional anomaly, with the 3L1S model being favored by $Δχ^2=15.1$. Under the favored 3L1S interpretation, the anomaly arises from a caustic induced by a planetary-mass companion, whereas the prominent caustic-crossing features are produced by the underlying binary lens. Combining the measured event timescale, $t_{\rm E}=7.55\pm0.30$ days, and angular Einstein radius, $θ_{\rm E}=0.325 \pm 0.059$ mas, with a Bayesian analysis, we infer a lens system consisting of an M dwarf of mass

2611.19117.title: Testing General Relativity by Reconstructing Dark Energy and the Growth Index with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
2611.19117.text: We extend the Cosmo-PINN, a physics-informed neural network for model-independent cosmological reconstruction, to reconstruct the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ and the growth index $γ(z)$ of matter perturbations. The reconstruction is performed through three modules: the background module, the matter growth module, and the growth index module. The background module learns the dark energy density $ρ_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ from cosmological observations, and $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ is reconstructed through the residual of the conservation equation. The reconstructed background is then passed to the other two modules, which reconstruct the observables $f(z)$ and $fσ_{8}(z)$ either directly from the linear perturbation equation of General Relativity or through an independently reconstructed growth index $γ(z)$. Comparing the two reconstructions on the same background p

2611.19048.title: Nearby M&M Binaries Uncovered with the Gaia Multipeak Fraction and Speckle Interferometry
2611.19048.text: Multipeak fraction is a strong indicator of stellar multiplicity with subarcsecond angular separation in the Gaia DR3 catalog. We select 18 sources with multipeak fraction above 5% among stars possibly in the 20 pc solar neighborhood with as yet unconfirmed binarity. We successfully resolve eleven systems of M-type dwarf components in speckle interferometric observations with a 2.5 m telescope at the Caucasian Mountain Observatory of Sternberg Astronomical Institute, Moscow State University. The tentatively estimated companion masses lie in the 0.09 -- 0.23 $M_\odot$ range. All six sources with a multipeak fraction of 6--8% are unresolved, suggesting an observational bias that affects nearby stars.

2611.19006.title: Cosmography with gravitational waves II: Padé approximants in an extended redshift regime
2611.19006.text: We evaluate the capability of next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, including LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and DECIGO, to probe cosmographic parameters using electromagnetically bright standard sirens. Adopting Padé approximants, we extend the cosmographic analysis to substantially higher redshifts and constrain the parameters $H_0$, $q_0$, $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$. We examine the constraints primarily as a function of the number of detections and, in a complementary analysis, across correlated SNR--redshift regimes. LISA provides percent-level constraints on $H_0$, while the Einstein Telescope and DECIGO reach subpercent precision as the catalogue size increases. The parameter $q_0$ can be constrained at the tens-of-percent level, whereas the higher-order parameters $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$ remain progressively less determined. Compared with the low-redshift Taylor analysis, the

2611.18980.title: Gradients of Turbulent Fluctuations as New Tracers of Astrophysical Magnetic Fields
2611.18980.text: Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is ubiquitous in astrophysical plasmas and produces scale-dependent anisotropy with respect to the local magnetic field. Because turbulence cascades preferentially perpendicular to the field, its spatial gradients acquire preferred orientations that can be used to probe magnetic-field structure. This property underlies a family of gradient techniques based on spectroscopic, synchrotron-intensity, and synchrotron-polarization observations. In this review, we summarize the theoretical foundation of these techniques, including the anisotropy of MHD turbulence and the corresponding behavior of velocity, magnetic-field, and density fluctuations. We then describe how these fluctuations are encoded in spectroscopic data and synchrotron observables, and review the implementation of Velocity Centroid Gradients, Velocity Channel Gradients, Intensity Gradients,

2611.18943.title: Developing a Sky-End Fibre Aperture for the AMASE Fibre Bundle
2611.18943.text: The Affordable Multiple-Aperture Spectroscopy Explorer (AMASE) project aims to enable high-resolution spectroscopy of ionised gas in galaxies. However, fabricating ultra- dense fibre bundles with micrometre-level precision presents significant challenges. We detail a fabrication process that combines precision machining, stress-reducing handling, and iterative polishing. Although the final prototype did not meet the optical performance targets, our methods reduced manual labour, improved reproducibility, and identified critical failure modes, providing essential information for future astrophotonic instrument designs.

2611.18929.title: Quantifying the Dominance and Emergence of Brightest Cluster Galaxies in SPT and Planck Clusters: A Novel Application of the Gini Index
2611.18929.text: We introduce the Gini index (G) as a metric for studying the emergence of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) by quantifying the disparity in the light distribution of galaxy cluster cores. The Gini index collapses the skewness of the bright-end luminosity function to a single statistic, and provides a measure for the light dominance of the BCG over other cluster members that is more robust than the magnitude gap. We argue that the Gini index is far less sensitive to short-term changes in the cluster dynamical state than the magnitude gap and solves its known degeneracies by taking the entire cluster membership into account, making G a more sensitive metric to long-term BCG assembly. We apply the magnitude gap and Gini index to a progenitor-selected sample of 92 South Pole Telescope- and Planck-selected cluster cores at 0 < z < 1 with corresponding Hubble Space Telescope F110W and F200LP a

2611.18904.title: Mid-Infrared Variability as a Probe of Hidden AGN Activity: A Comparison of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 AGNs in the BAT 58-Month Sample
2611.18904.text: In accordance with the AGN Unification model, the optical variability of Seyfert 2s is expected to be suppressed because the central engine is obscured by a dusty torus. The absorbed UV/optical radiation is reprocessed and re-emitted in longer wavelengths including the mid-infrared (MIR), making MIR variability a promising probe of obscured AGNs. We investigate the optical ASAS-SN and MIR NEOWISE variability of Seyfert 1 and Seyfert 2 AGNs from the \textit{Swift} 58-month BAT catalog, comparing both populations against non-variable galaxies. One of the first systematic studies of MIR AGN variability, we detected significant variability for Sy1s and the majority of Sy2s. 65% of Sy2s exhibit variability as significant as Sy1s in the MIR, especially in the W2 band, indicating torus dominated MIR variability. Additionally, 22% of Sy2s show higher variability compared to non-variable sources

2611.18876.title: Searching for Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence with SPT-3G
2611.18876.text: We search for anisotropic cosmic birefringence using two years of data from the SPT-3G instrument on the South Pole Telescope. Anisotropic cosmic birefringence refers to a theorized dependence of the refractive index of the vacuum on the polarization of light that varies across the Universe in a statistically isotropic manner. Such an effect would manifest as a direction-dependent mixing of the $E$ and $B$ polarization modes of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), caused by rotation of the polarization angle as photons travel from the CMB last scattering surface to us. We present a measurement of the power spectrum of the rotation angle $α$ in six bins across the angular multipole range $20 < L < 2048$, finding no evidence for cosmic birefringence with the spectrum consistent with zero. At 95% confidence, we set a new best upper limit on the amplitude of a scale-invariant birefringence

2611.18850.title: Interpreting JWST UV luminosity functions and angular correlation functions via a "universal language" for high-redshift galaxies
2611.18850.text: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) found more bright $z\gtrsim10$ galaxies than expected before its launch. No consensus has emerged on whether difficulties in reproducing them stem from missing physics, simplifying assumptions that break down at the highest redshifts, or model mis-calibration. This is complicated because most galaxy models cannot be compared like-to-like, and models invoking different physical processes can make similar predictions for compressed summaries such as ultraviolet luminosity functions (UV LFs). Here we describe galaxy populations in a universal language: a chain of physically and empirically motivated conditional distributions linking halo mass, stellar mass, star formation rate and UV magnitude, defined consistently across models and data. We build a broad prior from fits to five hydrodynamic simulations, which predict very different high-redshift galaxy

2611.18833.title: Black Hole Superradiance and the Gravitational Auger Effect
2611.18833.text: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of nature's light degrees of freedom. In the vicinity of a spinning black hole, it exponentially amplifies ultralight bosons from vacuum fluctuations to a macroscopic cloud of enormous occupation number. Observational superradiance effects - modified black-hole spins, gravitational-wave and coherent boson emission - are known to depend sensitively on bosonic self-interactions as induced by a quartic, $λφ^4$. Here we point out that purely gravitational interactions within the cloud significantly modify superradiance dynamics, through an analog of the Auger effect. Moreover, we identify nontrivial evolution of the superradiant levels beyond the first, driven by scattering into even higher levels and their radial overtones. doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb7e7.title: NEFERTITI : Linking Early Galaxy Formation to the Assembly of the Milky Way
doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb7e7.text: We use a new implementation of the NEFERTITI galaxy formation model, coupled to ∼30 high-resolution Caterpillar dark-matter simulations of Milky Way (MW) analogs, to connect early galaxy formation with the MW's assembly down to z = 0. Our locally constrained model resolves minihalos hosting the first Population III (Pop III) stars and self-consistently tracks inhomogeneous ionization and chemical enrichment. Pop III star formation begins at z ≃ 27, peaks at z ≃ 10–15, and persists down to z ≲ 5, producing Pop III systems with M * ∼ 10–5 × 10 5 M ⊙ . The present-day descendants of Pop III stars span [Fe/H] < −9 to ≈−1, with the most metal-poor stars typically enriched by a few (1–4) low-energy supernova progenitors. Pair-instability supernova descendants more commonly form in massive halos ( M vir > 10 8 M ⊙ ), often externally enriched, reflecting the strong feedback and delayed recovery

doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb021.title: Tracing Radial Structures of Molecular Gas and Gas-phase Metallicity across the Galaxy Merger Sequence with KILOGAS
doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb021.text: Galaxy interactions and mergers are expected to redistribute baryons across galactic disks, yet how molecular gas and metals are reorganized as a function of merger stage remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the radial structure of molecular gas and gas-phase metallicity (oxygen abundance traced by O3N2 ) using a large sample of nearby galaxies from the Kiloparsec Investigations of Local Objects’ Gas And Star formation (KILOGAS) survey spanning a wide range of interaction stages. We construct galaxy-by-galaxy radial profiles of molecular gas surface density and metallicity and characterize their shapes. We find that a significant fraction of gas-rich, star-forming galaxies, regardless of merger stage, deviates from simple single-slope profiles, and that molecular gas and metallicity do not always evolve in a coupled manner. doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb2de.title: Ultraviolet and Optical Signatures of Late-time Disk Instabilities in Tidal Disruption Events
doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb2de.text: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) are unique probes of evolving accretion in supermassive black holes (BHs). Recent models of TDE disks show that they undergo brief thermal instabilities with temporal super-Eddington accretion at late times, which has been suggested as a possibility to explain the ubiquitous late radio emergence in TDEs. We model the ultraviolet (UV) and optical signatures of such disk instabilities, expected from the accretion power being reprocessed by the optically thick outflow following super-Eddington accretion. Our model predicts brief UV-bright transients lasting for days, with luminosities of 10 42 –10 43 erg s −1 in the near-UV and 10 41 –10 42 erg s −1 in the optical for a typical TDE by a 10 6 M ⊙ BH. These could be detectable by near-future surveys such as ULTRASAT, the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and the Argus Array for TDEs at redshifts out to ≈0.1. We further

doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb014.title: Multiple H i 21 cm Absorbers Toward Blazar PKS 1158+007
doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb014.text: We report an interesting line of sight toward the blazar PKS 1158+007 (J1201+0028) ( z em = 1.369), revealing the rare detection of two intervening H i 21 cm absorption systems within a narrow redshift interval (Δ z ∼ 0.04) using the MeerKAT radio telescope. The stronger absorber at z abs = 0.5653 (∫ τdv = 1.31 ± 0.04 km s −1 ) is associated with a strong Mg ii λ 2796 system seen in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectra, with rest-frame equivalent widths of W 2796 = 1.40 ± 0.07 Å and 1.21 ± 0.11 Å, respectively. In stark contrast, the second detection at z abs = 0.5305 reveals a distinct H i 21 cm absorption feature (∫ τdv = 0.31 ± 0.04 km s −1 ) with no associated metal absorption detectable in the optical spectra. This system represents a prime example of a “metal-poor” H i 21 cm absorber. Using photometric redshifts from Hyper Supr

doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb87b.title: The Milky Way’s Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. II. The Multicomponent Age–Metallicity Structure of the High- α Disk
doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aeb87b.text: Whether the high- α disk experienced a continuous or episodic star formation history remains an open question. Here we investigate the age–metallicity distribution of the high- α disk using approximately 145,000 Gaia Data Release 3 subgiants with [Fe/H] > −1, 6.5 ≲ R ≲ 9.5 kpc, and ∣ Z ∣ ≲ 1.5 kpc. We adopt a forward-modelling framework that accounts for individual age and metallicity uncertainties and corrects for sample-selection effects. The reconstructed distribution reveals two components: a broad, dominant population peaking at ∼10.6 Gyr and [Fe/H] ≃ −0.38, and an older, more metal-poor population peaking at ∼12.4 Gyr and [Fe/H] ≃ −0.79. These features suggest an episodic history of star formation and chemical enrichment in the high- α disk, qualitatively consistent with cosmological simulations in which recurrent gas accretion drives variations in the star formation rate. doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202660169.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLIV. The first Euclid view of galaxy protocluster candidates at cosmic noon
doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202660169.text: A large catalogue of candidate galaxy protoclusters with high star formation rates (SFRs) was produced by the algorithm. This is an overdensity finder based on Delaunay tessellation that uses photometric redshift probability distributions through Monte Carlo simulations. Focussing our search on the eight highly star-forming < 2.7, and 12 of them also have partial ̋erschel coverage. All detections have also been confirmed by at least one other independent protocluster detection algorithm: Poisson Probability Method and Detection Algorithm for NAscent Structures (PPM-DIANAS). doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202662044.title: Parallel alignment of radio AGN jets and large cosmic web structures in the direction of the Shapley supercluster
doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202662044.text: We investigated the potential large-scale alignment of radio active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets in the proximity of the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) area and its correlation with the identified cosmic web structures. We analyzed 28 radio AGNs divided into two populations with comparable sky coverage north and south of a diffuse X-ray filamentary structure connecting clusters in the SSC core. We measured the average jet position angles (PAs) and combined them with spectroscopic redshifts to assess the persistence of the alignment along the line of sight. We detected a significant large-scale alignment of the radio AGN jets with the foreground X-ray filament (oriented at PA ∼ 115^ ̧irc ± 10^ ̧irc ). rss:universetoday:4883368d15b3163e4209b7.title: Did The First Quarks and Gluons Experience Brownian Motion? Sometimes.
rss:universetoday:4883368d15b3163e4209b7.text: The quark-gluon plasma of the early universe experienced Brownian motion, but a new theory predicts how a particle moving at close to the speed of light is likely to be pushed and pulled by a fluid as it flies through it. The result shows that Brownian statistics doesn't always apply.

rss:universetoday:397b557196b00ece87a148.title: China Signals Its Intention to Land on Jupiter's Moon Callisto
rss:universetoday:397b557196b00ece87a148.text: China is outlining plans to place a small lander on the surface of Jupiter's moon Callisto, the outermost of the four Galilean moons. It's an ambitious plan, and would be only the second time anything's landed on a Solar System body beyond Mars. But the payoff would be huge, even if the lander only carries its two proposed instruments.

rss:physorg:a3d6464f9c364d199bd14be9.title: Stellar pulsations reveal hidden 1.8-solar-mass companion
rss:physorg:a3d6464f9c364d199bd14be9.text: Massive stellar companions can be difficult to detect because they emit little visible light or show no obvious signs of accretion. Their gravitational pull, however, can be traced through the motion of nearby stars. In pulsating stars, regular brightness variations act as natural clocks, offering a way to find these hidden objects.

rss:physorg:846226bd3642716d538a6751.title: DESI weighs the Milky Way more precisely than ever
rss:physorg:846226bd3642716d538a6751.text: To estimate the Milky Way's mass, astronomers need to track the movements of stars and smaller satellite galaxies under its gravitational pull. The faster these objects travel at a given distance, the more mass is needed to hold them in place. For some time, these measurements have shown that most of our galaxy's mass can't be accounted for by the stars and gas we can see…

rss:universetoday:d192a972da475e87cf9a95.title: Galaxy Outflows Likely Regulate Star Formation At ‘Cosmic Noon’ NASA’s Webb Reveals
rss:universetoday:d192a972da475e87cf9a95.text: A galaxy’s ultimate habitability is likely linked to massive gaseous outflows that regulate star formation.

rss:nasa:a2ffe63805297beb312f88f9.text: For many astronauts, the spectacular sight of lightning stands out when looking back at Earth from the International Space Station.

rss:physorg:3161ed4a86aa341ca4518699.title: The sun, Earth, Jupiter and white dwarfs: Potential traps for dark matter
rss:physorg:3161ed4a86aa341ca4518699.text: Dark matter continues to evade direct detection. Its slower-moving particles might leave signals too faint for detectors to register, yet be more easily captured by planets and stars. As they accumulate inside these bodies, they could produce effects that existing instruments would allow us to search for.

rss:physorg:ba400f4b552fe44d8c2b6a94.title: Early black holes may have grown through productive chaos
rss:physorg:ba400f4b552fe44d8c2b6a94.text: When the universe was less than 700 million years old, the supermassive black hole powering a quasar called J0313-1806 had already grown to about 3 billion times the mass of the sun. It is one of the most extreme examples of a puzzle that has occupied astrophysicists for two decades: How did supermassive black holes grow so big so quickly?

rss:physorg:7ab275b46506ac7725cf3850.title: Euclid's H-alpha observations map where stars form in distant galaxies
rss:physorg:7ab275b46506ac7725cf3850.text: Euclid was launched into space in July 2023 to explore two of astronomy's biggest mysteries: dark matter and dark energy. The space telescope's first major data release covers some 1,900 square degrees of the sky, equivalent to around 14% of the area planned for the six-year mission and around 5% of the total sky. It is an unprecedented collection of visible and near-infrared observations.

2611.22952.title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
2611.22952.text: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 100 to 100,000 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. 2611.22914.title: FastSpecFit: Spectrophotometric Modeling of 38 Million Extragalactic Targets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Second Data Release
2611.22914.text: Optical spectrophotometry provides a direct window into the physical conditions, kinematics, and formation histories of galaxies and quasars. FastSpecFit is an open-source Python software package that forward-models each Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectrum jointly with its broadband photometry, convolving stellar-population synthesis and emission-line templates with each fiber's native spectral resolution. This forward-modeling approach preserves DESI's uncorrelated pixel statistics, fits a typical spectrum in ~0.1 s of single-core time, and scales to tens of millions of objects, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo resampling. 2611.22887.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- The evolution of the radio-loud AGN fraction-stellar mass relation to $z\sim3$ in the Euclid Deep Field North
2611.22887.text: The incidence of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (RLAGN) and their energetic output via AGN feedback are crucial in understanding the evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure of the Universe. In the local Universe, the incidence of RLAGN has been shown to correlate strongly with host galaxy properties, particularly stellar mass. Using the large-area survey capabilities provided by Euclid and the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR), we present the first study of the RLAGN incidence--stellar mass relation to $z=3.0$. We perform a stringent analysis accounting for cross-matching reliability and stellar-mass incompleteness. In addition, we test the robustness of our results against AGN and host galaxy classification. 2611.22771.title: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
2611.22771.text: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. 2611.22719.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
2611.22719.text: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $Ω_{gw}(f)/Ω_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. 2611.22618.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
2611.22618.text: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. 2611.22498.title: Using the 0i Einstein equation to break dark-sector degeneracies
2611.22498.text: Over the past decade, cosmological observations have started to challenge the $Λ$CDM model. If these tensions persist, they immediately raise one fundamental question: what new physics could be responsible for them? More specifically, do these deviations arise from a modification of gravity, from an evolving or clustering dark energy component, or from dark matter properties beyond the cold dark matter paradigm? In this paper we show that, with current methods, any observed deviation can always be attributed to more than one sector, preventing us from determining if the tension is due to gravity, dark energy or dark matter. The main reason is that current tests rely on unobservable quantities. These quantities are then either related to observables by assuming the validity of specific equations, or compared with theoretical predictions computed within a given class of theories. Both appr

2611.22487.title: Dual and Binary AGN at Cosmic Dawn: The need for a JWST Program to resolve the merger channel of Early Black Hole Growth
2611.22487.text: The discovery with JWST of accreting black holes (BHs) at z=4-9 in numbers far exceeding pre-JWST expectations, many of them overmassive relative to their hosts and linked to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), raises the question of how early BHs form and grow. Hierarchical assembly predicts that galaxy mergers drive gas to galactic nuclei and bring BHs together, leaving a direct observational signature: dual AGN at tens of kpc separations and sub-kpc to few-kpc "duets" in post-merger galaxies, which are the progenitors of the low-frequency GW sources targeted by pulsar timing arrays and LISA. 2611.22387.title: Probing Velocity-Dependent WIMP Dark Matter Annihilation in Large-Scale Structure
2611.22387.text: The unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) provides a promising avenue for probing the cosmological annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter through its cross-correlation with large-scale structure (LSS). While most previous studies have assumed a velocity-independent (s-wave) annihilation cross section, many well-motivated particle physics models predict annihilation rates that depend on the relative velocity of dark matter particles. In this work, we develop a generalized halo-model framework to investigate the cosmological signatures of velocity-dependent WIMP annihilation. Parameterizing the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section as $σv_{\rm rel}\propto v_{\rm rel}^{n}$, we consider four representative cases corresponding to Sommerfeld-like (n=-1), s-wave (n=0), p-wave (n=2), and d-wave (n=4) annihilation. 2611.22378.title: Bent-tailed radio galaxies as tracers of the intrafilament medium
2611.22378.text: Bent-tailed radio galaxies have traditionally been associated with, and used as tracers of, the dense intracluster medium. In recent years, however, such sources have also been identified outside of clusters, with only a few discovered in low-density environments of cosmic filaments. Their occurrence in low-density environments remains rare and is still poorly understood. We announce the discovery of bent-tailed radio galaxies in galaxy cluster filaments. We have identified two bent-tailed radio galaxies, J0020-25 and J0019-26, within a filament at the redshift of $z \sim 0.1273$, and another bent-tailed radio galaxy, J0019-25, in a separate filament at $z \sim 0.1126$. We used MeerKAT observations of these bent-tailed radio galaxies to place constraints on their intrafilament medium (IFM).
